options.title: Implement escalation huddles
options.description: Trigger escalation huddles when room-to-physician wait times exceed predefined thresholds, addressing slow physician pace and waiting room surges.
options.local_fit: This option aligns with the observed slow physician pace and potential waiting room surges, as suggested by the evidence. It provides a structured approach to managing these challenges.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: Implementing escalation huddles may shift pressure to the charge nurse, who will be responsible for convening and leading these meetings. This could alleviate some of the pressure on physicians, but it may also increase the charge nurse's workload.
options.how_we_would_know: Monitor the effectiveness of the huddles in reducing wait times and improving physician efficiency. Collect feedback from both charge nurses and physicians to assess the impact and make necessary adjustments.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If the huddles fail to show significant improvement or if physician pace remains consistently slow despite the huddles, reconsider the approach and explore alternative strategies.

options.title: Protect monitored beds for acute arrivals
options.description: Ensure a reserve of monitored beds is maintained for acute arrivals, especially during periods of high bed occupancy.
options.local_fit: Given the observed high bed occupancy, this option is relevant. It aims to address the issue of no monitored beds being available for acute arrivals.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: Implementing this process may shift pressure to the charge nurse, who will need to closely monitor bed availability and ensure the reserve is maintained. However, it could also alleviate pressure on physicians by providing them with the necessary resources to manage acute cases promptly.
options.how_we_would_know: Track the number of instances where monitored beds were successfully reserved for acute arrivals. Monitor wait times for these patients to ensure they receive timely care. Regularly assess the impact on bed occupancy and physician workload.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If the implementation of this process leads to consistently low bed availability or if it fails to improve the wait times for acute arrivals, reconsider the approach and explore other strategies.

options.title: Adjust rooming pace to clinician capacity
options.description: Monitor the rooming pace and adjust it based on clinician capacity, especially during periods of high bed occupancy.
options.local_fit: This option is relevant given the observed high bed occupancy and the potential for rooming to continue while physician pace slows. It aims to align rooming pace with clinician capacity.
options.possible_pressure_transfer: Adjusting the rooming pace may shift pressure to the charge nurse, who will need to closely monitor both rooming and clinician capacity. However, it could also alleviate pressure on physicians by ensuring they have the necessary time to manage each patient effectively.
options.how_we_would_know: Regularly monitor the rooming pace and compare it to clinician capacity. Assess the impact on wait times and patient flow. Collect feedback from both charge nurses and physicians to understand the effectiveness of the adjustments.
options.revisit_or_stop_if: If adjusting the rooming pace fails to show significant improvement or if it leads to consistently long wait times, reconsider the approach and explore alternative strategies.

recommendation.rationale: Given the observed high bed occupancy, protecting monitored beds for acute arrivals is a practical and immediate step to ensure timely care for these patients. While the evidence strength is low, the local fit is strong, suggesting this option is worth pursuing.
recommendation.would_change_if: If the evidence strength for this option increased, indicating a stronger correlation between high bed occupancy and slow physician pace, we would consider prioritizing it further. Additionally, if the local context changed, such as a significant increase in bed availability, we might reconsider the need for this intervention.

suggested_reviewers.why: Charge nurses are directly involved in managing bed occupancy and coordinating patient flow. Their insights are crucial for understanding the challenges and implementing effective solutions.
Physician leads can provide valuable insights into the challenges faced by physicians and offer suggestions for improving efficiency and wait times.
